UNITED STATES DISTRICT COURT
FOR THE EASTERN DISTRICT OF VIRGINIA
ALEXANDRIA DIVISION
MARVELLE J. BALLENTINE,
Plaintiff,
Case No. 1:26-cv-02331
V.
KATIE HALL, individually;
NATIONAL CENTER FOR MISSING & EXPLOITED
CHILDREN;
META PLATFORMS, INC.;
and JOHN/JANE DOES 1-6,
Defendants.
PROPOSED| ORDER B
(Granting Reconsideration in Part, Stating the Postponement of the Rule 26(f) Conference,
and Establishing the Procedure Following Disposition of the Pending Motions to Dismiss)
This matter is before the Court on Plaintiff's Rule 54(b) Motion to Reconsider ECF No.
108 as to ECF No. 105 (the "Motion"). Upon consideration of the Motion, the memorandum in
support, any response and reply, and the record, it is hereby
ORDERED as follows:
Disposition. The Motion is GRANTED IN PART, to the extent this Order clarifies
and modifies the disposition of Plaintiff's Motion for an Order Directing Completion of the Rule
26(f) Conference and Submission of a Discovery Plan (ECF No. 105) in the Order entered October
30, 2026 (ECF No. 108) and establishes the terms stated below. The Motion is otherwise DENIED
without prejudice.
1

Immediate deadline. Plaintiff's request for an immediate deadline to complete the
Rule 26(f) conference is DENIED without prejudice.
Postponement. The Court determines that planning must remain postponed. The
parties' conference under Federal Rule of Civil Procedure 26(f) and the written report under Rule
26(f)(2) are postponed pending disposition of the motions to dismiss at ECF Nos. 10, 21, and 45.
Disclosures and discovery. Initial disclosures under Rule 26(a)(1)(C) are not due
until a date set by further order. Any postponement of discovery is limited to the scope stated in
paragraph 5. This paragraph does not restrict informal investigation and does not displace any
order that separately authorizes discovery.
Source and scope. The postponement stated in paragraphs 3 and 4 rests on the
following direction or determination, which the Court states here, including the source and scope
of any direction of the District Judge on which the Court relies, or the Court's own determination
under Rule 26(f)(1):
6.
Preservation. Existing obligations to preserve discoverable information are not
modified by this Order. This Order imposes no additional preservation obligation.
7.
Status report. Within 14 days after disposition of the last of ECF Nos. 10, 21, and
45, unless a final judgment has ended the action, Plaintiff and counsel of record for each Defendant
remaining in the action shall file a joint status report.
8.
Contents. The status report shall identify: (a) the claims and parties remaining in
the action; (b) any leave to amend granted and the deadline for the amended pleading; (c) proposed
2

dates for the Rule 26(f) conference, the written report, and initial disclosures; and (d) any
continuing request for postponement and the grounds for it.
9.
Individual report. A party unable to obtain a joint status report shall file its own
status report by the deadline in paragraph 7.
10.
Partial disposition. After a ruling on fewer than all of ECF Nos. 10, 21, and 45,
any party may move for earlier planning as to the claims and parties that remain. Such a motion
does not itself impose planning obligations on any party whose motion to dismiss remains
undecided.
11.
Effect of a status report. The filing of a status report under this Order does not
commence discovery and does not modify paragraph 4.
12.
Other matters. Except as this Order expressly provides, ECF No. 108, including
its disposition of ECF No. 103, ECF No. 84, and every other order remain unchanged, and every
pending motion, objection, and application remains pending on its own grounds.
Alexandria, Virginia
_ 2026
William E. Fitzpatrick
United States Magistrate Judge
